fields.description: Ruijie controllers log customers in through RADIUS. Bandofy runs its own RADIUS server (bench execute bandofy.radius_server.start, see docs/ruijie.md); it accepts only the one-time logins Bandofy issues after a payment, voucher or free trial.
fields.label: Bandofy RADIUS Server

fields.description: While off, the RADIUS server rejects every login.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: The key in `radius-server host <Bandofy IP> key <secret>` on every Ruijie controller. Use a long random value: sites behind mobile-network NAT can't be told apart by IP, so this secret is what admits them.
fields.label: RADIUS Shared Secret

fields.description: Accept the controller's MAC-based re-login (dot1x-mab) for a device whose paid time hasn't run out, so it reconnects without the portal. The device is trusted by its MAC, as on Omada sites.
fields.label: Allow MAC Re-login

fields.description: After a customer pays, the portal sends Bandofy's one-time username and password to the controller's own login server, which then asks the RADIUS server above. Placeholders: {username}, {password}, {user_ip}, {user_mac}, {ac_name}, {nas_ip}, {ap_mac}, {ssid}, {url} (where the customer was going) and {success_url}.
fields.label: Controller Login Page

fields.description: Must match `web-auth auth-server submit-url` on the controller.
fields.label: Login Submit URL

fields.description: Optional JSON object of more form fields to send, e.g. {"userip": "{user_ip}", "usermac": "{user_mac}"}. Check the field names your controller firmware expects.
fields.label: Extra Fields
